patients.label: Case: 35-year-old G4P3 pregnant woman at 28 weeks of gestation with gestational diabetes mellitus, polyhydramnios and a foetus with congenital diaphragmatic hernia and trisomy 18

identity_evidence.quote: A 35-year-old G4P3 lady at 28 weeks of gestation

attribution_limitations: The first scan reports that a stomach bubble was absent and that the stomach bubble was noted in the thoracic cavity; the discussion repeats both. The source does not say the absence refers to the abdomen, so both are kept as written without a stated link.

Polyhydramnios severity is described as moderate-to-severe in the introduction and moderate in the discussion, with a deepest vertical pocket of 12 cm and a later amniotic fluid index of 43 cm. No severity grade is assigned to any fact.

Edwards syndrome is described as suggested by the karyotype and consistent with the findings in the case text, but the introduction says the foetus has underlying Edwards syndrome. Only the karyotype-supported trisomy 18 is recorded as a confirmed condition.
The heart is recorded as normal in structure on the detailed scan while the first scan reports it pushed to the right side; the source does not say whether these refer to the same assessment.

The decision for expectant management and comfort care appears only in an unlabelled discussion sentence whose subject "they" has no literal antecedent naming this case's parents; kept review-only. Its timing relative to the follow-up and delivery is not stated.

Amnioreduction and the amniotic fluid index of 43 cm are placed only "during subsequent follow-up" with no named anchor or gestational age, so their order against the counselling is not stated; they precede the delivery only because amnioreduction is an antenatal procedure on the pregnancy.

evidence.quote: A 35-year-old G4P3 lady at 28 weeks of gestation came for a routine antenatal checkup.

In the present case, the patient was diagnosed with GDM at 18 weeks of gestation and polyhydramnios during a routine prenatal visit at 28 weeks of gestation. Polyhydramnios was the first suspicious sign the primary care medical officer noticed.
A 35-year-old G4P3 lady
A 35-year-old G4P3 lady
She was diagnosed with GDM at 18 weeks of gestation
She had no history of infection, osmotic diuresis or hypoglycaemic symptoms throughout her pregnancy.
Transabdominal ultrasound revealed polyhydramnios with a deepest vertical pocket (DVP) of 12 cm, suggesting a ‘uterus larger than date’.

In the present case, the patient was diagnosed with GDM at 18 weeks of gestation and polyhydramnios during a routine prenatal visit at 28 weeks of gestation. Polyhydramnios was the first suspicious sign the primary care medical officer noticed.
During subsequent follow-up, the patient had symptomatic polyhydramnios with an amniotic fluid index (AFI) of 43 cm and an amnioreduction was performed.

evidence.quote: A detailed scan by an MFM consultant revealed that the foetus had multiple anomalies such as left-side cleft lip, claw hand, rocker bottom feet, stomach bubble in the thoracic cavity with a lung-to-head ratio of 0.58 and polyhydramnios with a DVP of 12 cm which consistent with CDH.
In our case, the foetus was diagnosed with CDH and underlying trisomy 18 at 28 weeks of gestation, resulting in a fresh stillbirth delivery at 34 weeks of gestation.

claims.text: A 35-year-old G4P3 woman at 28 weeks of gestation attended a routine antenatal checkup. She had been diagnosed with gestational diabetes mellitus at 18 weeks and was on oral glucose-lowering drugs with suboptimised blood sugar profile monitoring, and she had no history of infection, osmotic diuresis or hypoglycaemic symptoms in the pregnancy. The marriage was non-consanguineous, the families had no history of congenital anomalies or syndromes, and her previous pregnancies were uneventful with healthy children.

claims.text: The symphysial fundal height was 31 cm and foetal parts were difficult to palpate. She was referred to an MFM consultant, whose detailed scan found left-side cleft lip, claw hand, rocker bottom feet and a lung-to-head ratio of 0.58, consistent with congenital diaphragmatic hernia. Amniocentesis karyotyping showed a male foetus with trisomy 18.
